races.name: www.mourneabbeyoil.ie Mares Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beechingstoke
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Andrew Slattery, placed twice from two hurdle runs both on good ground, handles the conditions fine but 65 days off and an amateur 7lb claimer in Josh Younge means any fitness shortfall could be exposed in a strongly-run 2m1f.

runners_data.name: Belladaball
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's consistent mare has winning and placed form on good ground over the right trip, but her natural hold-up style will be compromised in this field — she is a true closer who is likely to find herself further forward than ideal, tempering her finishing effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Easter Bonnet
runners_data.note: Willie Mullins mare with a hurdles win and strong placed efforts on good ground, prominent style suits a genuine gallop, and Brian Hayes claiming the ride for a yard firing at 11/54 in 14 days signals strong stable confidence; arguably the standout profile in this race shape.

runners_data.name: Emerald Enigma
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in two hurdle starts, both wins on good ground, Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins — a formidable combination; the confirmed front-runner whose ability to control tempo and quicken clear is the central factor this race revolves around.

runners_data.name: Flowing Fast
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and going preference unknown, recent form shows a fall and a pull-up which are serious concerns in a 20-runner field; the amateur 7lb claimer adds further risk and this runner must be treated with real caution.

runners_data.name: Fraher Field
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse for the Kiely yard with good ground form over the right distances, but the redistribution into midfield means she is unlikely to get a clear run from her natural position; 17 days since last run is fine but the crowded field is a significant obstacle.

runners_data.name: Golden Wings
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's mare has a hold-up style tagged with a fading flag, and on heavy-side good form figures she has rarely troubled the judge in similar conditions; Jack Kennedy is a major positive but the horse's tendency to fade and being pushed forward of her natural spot are real negatives.

runners_data.name: Jolly D'olivate
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up mare with a fades flag and recent form of 9th and 8th, 11 days since her last run is quick turnaround and nothing in her record suggests she can win at this level on this going.

runners_data.name: Kaleo Ametsa
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type for Josh Halley with five recent starts on good ground, all placed or fifth at best and no win — she shows up but does not win, and that pattern is hard to ignore even with the right conditions.

runners_data.name: Kauto Empress
runners_data.note: Lightly raced, sole run produced a 10th on good ground and she fades in the finish; the amateur 7lb claimer and unknown quantity make her an extreme risk in a competitive 20-runner field.

runners_data.name: Queenofqueenstreet
runners_data.note: 388 days off the track for E Sheehy, only run was a 15th on good ground 17f, fades flag, and a long lay-off into a 20-runner maiden hurdle does not inspire confidence regardless of conditions.

runners_data.name: The Orphan Girl
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with going preference unknown but flat form string of 6-4-3-4-1 suggests she is improving and has winning ability; Peter Fahey yard and an amateur claimer in Ethan O'Sullivan, trip step-up is the key unknown on return from 149 days off.

runners_data.name: Windy Grey
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with fades flag, form figures of 8th and a pulled-up effort on soft and heavy, 130 days off the track, and an amateur 7lb claimer — multiple concerns stack up and the step to good ground is untested.

runners_data.name: Wonderful Everyday
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Mullins with Danny Mullins aboard, has shown ability to place but struggles to win from the lead; the danger is she does the donkey work for Emerald Enigma and empties in the closing stages having set the pace throughout.

runners_data.name: Absolutley Fab
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a single run showing 12th on good ground, the fades flag is already established; her natural hold-up tendency means she is unlikely to get anywhere near her preferred trailing position in this large field, and nothing in her profile demands attention at this stage.

runners_data.name: Kenny's Jewel
runners_data.note: Margaret Mullins's four-year-old with J J Slevin aboard is a positive jockey booking, but recent form is a pull-up, 8th and an 11th, and the fades flag suggests she lacks the resolution to get competitive from off the pace in 2m1f.

runners_data.name: Misty Valentine
runners_data.note: A four-year-old with a single pulled-up run on good ground, natural hold-up style, and a 7lb amateur claimer — virtually no evidence base to assess and should be treated as a maiden in the fullest sense.

runners_data.name: Neat As A Pin
runners_data.note: Emer Bolger's four-year-old has unseated and finished 12th in two starts, fades consistently, and 13 days since last run does not suggest a dramatic bounce-back; nothing in the profile warrants shortening the odds.

runners_data.name: Thelittleredfox
runners_data.note: Sole run was 12th on good ground at 17f, going preference uncertain, fades flag already noted, and no jockey declared — the absence of a jockey listing is itself a red flag for market movers.

runners_data.name: Sea Limit
runners_data.note: Going preference entirely unknown from lightly raced profile, 113 days off the track, no jockey declared, and the six-year-old's only visible form figure is a 6th — essentially an unknown quantity in a race with several far better-defined profiles.

races.paceDynamic: Wonderful Everyday and Emerald Enigma are the two confirmed front-runners in a 20-runner mares maiden, and with both likely to press from the front, this race will be run at an honest, genuine gallop from the outset rather than a crawl that collapses late. Emerald Enigma, partnered by Paul Townend and unbeaten in two hurdles runs on good ground, is the classier of the two pace-setters and will not relinquish the lead cheaply; Wonderful Everyday has the profile of a willing but ultimately limited front-runner who has rarely won from the front. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can realistically get their preferred positions — Golden Wings, Belladaball, Absolutley Fab and Fraher Field are true hold-up horses who will be shuffled further forward than ideal, while Easter Bonnet and Beechingstoke are genuine prominent types who should be close enough to capitalise if the pace causes attrition. A genuine gallop on good ground over 2m1f at Cork strongly favours horses who can race prominently and sustain their effort into the straight, rather than closers who will find traffic and distance to make up after being compressed into midfield.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Emerald Enigma Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Emerald Enigma dictates a strong but measured pace from the front and kicks off the home turn.
scenarios.body: Townend allows Emerald Enigma to stride clear at her own tempo, and her unbeaten hurdles record on good ground suggests she has enough class to repel all challengers in the straight; the honest gallop set by Wonderful Everyday simply ensures rivals are kept honest rather than able to produce a sprint finish. Prominent racers who track the pace closely without over-racing are best placed, with Easter Bonnet ideally suited having won on similar ground.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Two Fight, Gaps Appear
scenarios.trigger: If Wonderful Everyday and Emerald Enigma race hard against each other early, setting a punishing tempo that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: The two leaders push each other through the early stages, and the relentless gallop causes enough attrition that one or both tire in the closing stages, opening the door for a prominent racer travelling strongly just off the pace. Easter Bonnet and Beechingstoke, both comfortable racing close to a strong gallop, are best equipped to pounce if the leaders blunder or weaken at the final flight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Threads Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to string the field out and a horse from midfield finds clear daylight to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: The genuine gallop does create room for a sustained late run if traffic breaks correctly, but most of the horses with a genuine hold-up profile have been mapped into midfield due to overcrowding at the rear, meaning this scenario relies partly on horses racing out of role. Belladaball or Fraher Field, the most experienced of the redistributed hold-up types, would need a seamless passage to get competitive from where they are likely to find themselves.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Finish, Field Bunches
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves uneven or the leaders capitulate, compressing the field into a messy finish around the home turn.
scenarios.body: With 20 runners, a crowded home straight is plausible if any fallers or interference disrupt the flow, and in that scenario a horse with tactical versatility who avoids trouble benefits most. Easter Bonnet's proven ability to race prominently and quicken, and Beechingstoke's consistent placed efforts, give them the adaptability to benefit from a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Watch Emerald Enigma's jumping — if she makes an error at a hurdle while on the front end, the race opens dramatically and a prominent racer like Easter Bonnet would inherit a winning position immediately.

The 20-runner field creates significant traffic risk around Cork's turning track; hold-up horses like Belladaball and Fraher Field, forced further forward than their natural style, may still get impeded when the field compresses entering the home straight.

Wonderful Everyday could set a pace that flatters Emerald Enigma entirely — if the two front-runners split wide or race hard at each other in the first mile, watch for Wonderful Everyday to capitulate from the home turn.
Two runners have no jockey declared — Thelittleredfox and Sea Limit — making any late market moves on either suspicious and worth monitoring before the off.

Easter Bonnet is 24 days off her last run for a Mullins yard striking at 11/54 in the past fortnight; that combination of form, going, prominent style and jockey booking (Brian Hayes) makes her a benchmark horse whose pre-race price movement is worth tracking.

races.name: John O'Flynn Motors 110 Series Final Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Arctic Flame
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up performer with strong similar-going form (2W5P on Good), trainer Foley pair both freshened on 24-day break; needs a decent enough gallop to deliver his finishing effort from the rear, and the controlled pace here is a slight concern for him getting back in time.
runners_data.comment: Arctic Flame arrives on the back of a win last time out, with a second two starts back underscoring her consistency, and experience over today's trip and going stands her in good stead; the chief concern is a hefty 166 lb to carry.

runners_data.name: Eastmore
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with an outstanding Good-ground record (14/15 similar-going starts with 2W8P), C Byrnes runner arrives off 32 days but has been placed five times on Good at distances fitting this trip; ideally placed to travel in second or third throughout.
runners_data.comment: Eastmore won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but he's finished second or third in four of his last five starts, suggesting he flirts with winning without always delivering — and 164 lb could test him here.

runners_data.name: Let's Go La Fichad
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner — won over 18f on Good last time out (7 days ago), and with no rival willing or able to press him he can control the pace entirely; his Going record here is more limited (2/6) so he is not unbeatable but this race shape is clearly built around him.
runners_data.comment: Won two starts back and returns quickly on familiar distance and going, giving Let's Go La Fichad a solid profile under a big 160 lb burden. The trainer's current 0/22 run of form is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: In The Trenches
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's hold-up type arrives on a 10-day turnaround with a win and place in similar going; ran a 4th over 19f on Good last time and will need to be produced late — he is genuine back-of-the-field territory and the uncontested pace from the front is a mild concern.
runners_data.comment: In The Trenches won three starts back and was second four starts back, giving him a solid recent profile over today's trip and going, and our rating just edges him to the top of this field; the in-form concern is a trainer cold streak to note.

runners_data.name: Gino Bella
runners_data.note: Foley's second string wears headgear (ht) and races prominently; won last time on Good over 17f 24 days ago and is clearly in form — the T14 0/3 read across both Foley runners, but Gino Bella's own recent form and prominent style suit this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Gino Bella won last time out and has experience of today's distance and going, but her pulling up three starts back casts a question mark over her reliability, and carrying 157 lb is a stiff ask for a mare ranked mid-field here.

runners_data.name: Dairy Force
runners_data.note: Jack Kennedy takes the ride for Gordon Elliott (T14 2/41 good recent form), and this seven-year-old has been placed five times on Good ground; a prominent racer who rarely wins outright (one win in last 15 similar-going starts) but consistently features and is dangerous here in scenario A.
runners_data.comment: Dairy Force has run over today's trip and going, and a second two starts back hints at ability, but he was fifth last time out, his trainer is in poor form at 2/41 over the past fortnight, and he remains winless in his last five starts — a tough ask off 155 lb.

runners_data.name: Quint Major
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up type who has struggled for a win recently (best finish in last 5 is a 4th), carries 154lbs and sits OR 104; form string shows a 7th last time on Good over 16f and offers little appeal unless this becomes a very rough tactical race.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, Quint Major does at least return quickly on seven days' rest and has run over today's distance and going before; a fourth three starts back shows some ability, though he carries 154 lb from a midfield ranking.

runners_data.name: Metamorpheus
runners_data.note: Andrew McNamara runner arrives on just a 2-day turnaround — an unusually quick reappearance — and is a hold-up type with placed form on Good (2/17f, 4/18f); his freshness must be questioned but he is relatively lightly weighted at 153lbs and could outrun his odds if the pace suits late runners.
runners_data.comment: Metamorpheus has been consistently knocking on the door — second last time out, and a second three starts back — and with experience over today's trip and going, he shapes as a genuine danger off a mark of 103. The risk is a run just two days ago.

runners_data.name: Kilt
runners_data.note: Rothwell's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up type by inclination — his win came over 17f on Good from the back — but the congested field means he is unlikely to settle at the very rear; STYLE_FIT 0.91 flags a slightly compromised position, though his Going record (13/15 similar going) is strong and he should not be dismissed.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in his last two starts and ranked 11th of 12 on our figures, Kilt is hard to fancy despite the win three starts back; he has run over today's trip and going, and 18 days off leaves him fresh enough, but the weight of 148 lb adds no help.

runners_data.name: Le Diablo
runners_data.note: A naturally rear-travelling horse whose best form (3rd, 2nd) has come settling deep; JJ Slevin takes the ride for John Patrick Ryan, and while his 12/12 similar-going record is excellent, the redistribution means he will likely race closer than ideal — STYLE_FIT 0.92 tempers his chance if the front runners control things.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked tenth of twelve on our figures, Le Diablo faces a stiff ask here; he has run over today's trip and going before, and back-to-back placed efforts latterly at least suggest some consistency, but 148 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Midnight Eagle
runners_data.note: McNamara's second runner carries the fades-in-finish flag alongside a redistribution note — a hold-up type in nature who will likely race closer to midfield than usual; recent form (2nd over 17f on Good) is solid but the style mismatch and the tendency to weaken late make this a risky proposition here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked ninth of twelve on our figures, Midnight Eagle faces a stiff ask here; experience over today's trip and going is in her favour, and a second last time out plus a third three starts back show she can find the frame, though 146 lb makes life harder still.

runners_data.name: Max Meridius
runners_data.note: Thomas Mullins's five-year-old won last time over 18f on Good but his overall similar-going record (6/14) is modest; tagged both fades-in-finish and redistributed, meaning he will race closer than suits him and may not deliver his finishing effort at the right moment — Danny Mullins rides but the flags stack against him.
runners_data.comment: Max Meridius landed a win in his last five starts but has otherwise shown little consistency — unplaced efforts dominate his recent record — and ranked last on our figures, he faces a stiff ask here, though he has run over today's trip and going before.

races.paceDynamic: Let's Go La Fichad is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no obvious challenger likely to press him hard from the outset, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m1f trip on Good ground at Cork. With Eastmore, Gino Bella, and Dairy Force likely to track in prominent positions, a small cluster will sit within striking range throughout, meaning this is a moderately-paced affair rather than a truly pressured test. The majority of the remaining field — Arctic Flame, In The Trenches, Metamorpheus, and others — are genuine hold-up horses who will be hunting the leaders from midfield to two out before the final exchanges. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel in behind Let's Go La Fichad without using excess energy, then produce a sustained run from the second-last — the most likely beneficiaries are those racing in the second tier (P) rather than those launching from deep. Several horses in this field are natural hold-up types — Kilt, Le Diablo, Midnight Eagle, and Max Meridius — who have been mapped to midfield because the field cannot accommodate all of them at the rear; of these, Kilt and Le Diablo carry the highest STYLE_FIT scores and are most likely to press forward and actually secure a nearer position than their redistribution tag implies.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Go La Fichad sets a fair, uncontested gallop and the race is won by a horse travelling prominently throughout.
scenarios.body: Let's Go La Fichad dictates throughout at a fair pace, and one of the prominent trio — Eastmore, Gino Bella, or Dairy Force — travels smoothly in his wake before asserting from the second-last hurdle; the lack of genuine pace pressure means their energy reserves are intact for the finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Collects Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is sufficient to string out the field and a horse from the chasing pack produces the strongest late run.
scenarios.body: A fair clip from the front means the leaders use enough to allow a well-handicapped hold-up type like Arctic Flame or In The Trenches to reel them in on the run-in after the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Defies Field
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Go La Fichad dictates a very modest tempo and none of the prominent horses have enough pace to reel him in.
scenarios.body: Ross O'Sullivan's five-year-old, who came here off just a seven-day turnaround in good form (1st last time out), simply allows the others to fight among themselves and slips away; on Good ground over 2m1f at Cork he has already won at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrambled Finish, Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If there is notable interference, falls, or the pace collapses causing a bunched finish from which an unexpected hold-up type arrives late.
scenarios.body: A compressed mid-race pace creates a traffic-clogged scenario where Metamorpheus or Le Diablo, both held up and carrying lower weights, find room late to challenge; the redistributed hold-up horses racing out of role make this shape less reliable than the probabilities for the prominent-style scenarios.

watchPoints.text: Let's Go La Fichad — if he is allowed to slip the field after the last hurdle with no pressure applied, the entire race could be over before the prominent horses can react; watch his stride pattern from the third-last.

Eastmore and Gino Bella — both Patrick Foley-trained prominent horses may jostle for the same ground behind Let's Go La Fichad in the early stages; any interference between them in the first mile could compromise the pair.

Metamorpheus — arriving on just a 2-day turnaround for Andrew McNamara is highly unusual and bears watching in the parade ring; if he shows any sign of sourness or fatigue pre-race, discount him significantly.

Kilt and Le Diablo — both are genuine back-to-front horses being pushed forward by field congestion; watch whether either settles comfortably in midfield or fights for position, as their ability to relax will dictate how much finishing energy they retain.

Jack Kennedy (Dairy Force) — top jockey booking for a Gordon Elliott handicapper with the trainer in good recent form (T14 2/41); a confident early move to track the leader could signal stable confidence and would accelerate Scenario A considerably.

races.name: Follow Us On Instagram Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners_data.name: Two Can Plan
runners_data.note: Holds an OR of 97 and is the highest-rated runner in the field, but has shown a preference for 2m+ on soft ground and his form string of P067P reads poorly; Andrew Slattery yard is 3/34 in the last 14 days and he has been off 101 days, making his sharpness a genuine question on return.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up on two of those occasions, Two Can Plan is a 101-day absence and 166 lb to overcome; he has run over today's trip, though his recent profile offers limited encouragement.

runners_data.name: Pirate Island
runners_data.note: Sean Flanagan takes the ride on this hold-up type who has placed five times in 15 runs on Good ground without winning; the 91-day break is a concern in a competitive handicap, though James Hannon's yard has not had a runner in the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Pirate Island has a win among his last five starts and has run over today's trip and going, while our rating just edges him to the top of this field — the concern is a lengthy 91-day absence and the burden of 162 lb.

runners_data.name: Midnight Musical
runners_data.note: Anthony McCann's five-year-old was seen 28 days ago and has placed once in seven Good-ground runs; a flag for fading in the finish is a material concern in a 2m1f stamina test, and the hold-up style is at odds with the slow pace this race shape is likely to generate.
runners_data.comment: Ranked second of 18 in our assessment and boasting experience over today's trip and conditions, Midnight Musical arrives 28 days fresh and well-weighted at 161 lb — a genuine danger; the risk is that she's winless in her last five starts.

runners_data.name: Toon Town
runners_data.note: Shane O'Callaghan takes the ride on a nine-year-old who has won and placed multiple times on Good, and his record of 1W2P in seven Good-ground runs is respectable; a hold-up horse in profile but his recent win at 2m4f and ability to place from off the pace makes him suited to a compressed finish if pace is slow.
runners_data.comment: Toon Town won last time out and has experience of today's trip and going, but 74 days off the track raises a fitness query and 160 lb is a hefty burden for a gelding rated 91 officially.

runners_data.name: Let It Settle
runners_data.note: Phillip Enright rides a lightly-raced five-year-old who was out just 11 days ago; placed once in eleven Good-ground runs and the form string of 00-026 reflects inconsistency, though the recent second over 2m1f on Good is directly relevant form for this contest.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, though her second two runs back offers encouragement, and she has run over today's trip and going; 159 lb is a stern ask, but an 11-day turnaround suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Inchiquin Maid
runners_data.note: Terence O'Brien's mare last ran 27 days ago and has form of 0W3P in 15 Good-ground outings; her natural style is as a true hold-up horse but in an 18-runner field she is realistically going to find herself in midfield rather than the rear, which slightly improves her position if pace is slow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Inchiquin Maid does bring placed efforts — second two and three starts back — though a fifth last time out is less encouraging; she has run over today's trip and going, and 157 lb could anchor her in midfield.

runners_data.name: Mambo Du Large
runners_data.note: Tom Kelly (7lb claimer) rides a four-year-old who has run three times on Good ground and never placed; the hold-up profile means this lightly-raced juvenile will need a strongly-run race to deliver from off the pace, and the experience deficit in a large competitive field is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Mambo Du Large is yet to win in his last four starts, but remains lightly raced and unexposed, with scope for better — 24 days between runs suggests he arrives here fresh, and carrying 157 lb, connections clearly retain faith.

runners_data.name: Taketwotoone
runners_data.note: Runs for T O'Connor and was last seen 18 days ago; a natural hold-up horse who also carries a fades-in-finish flag, and the combination of racing out of role in a compressed field while not seeing out the trip makes this a difficult win-prospect, however his Good-ground record has two placed efforts from nine.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, including back-to-back unplaced efforts before sixth and eighth-place finishes, Taketwotoone faces a stiff task in a field of eighteen, though she has run over today's trip before and a rating of 89 keeps her competitive on paper.

runners_data.name: Saint Peregrine
runners_data.note: John Aherne (7lb) keeps the ride for John Patrick Ryan, who is 1/16 in the last 14 days; the prominent style makes him one of the few runners who can genuinely track Eaglewood, though his Good-ground record of 0W3P from 15 and form of 7F0-09 is modest and the fall on that form string is a safety note over hurdles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Saint Peregrine nonetheless catches the eye on a our rating of 98 that puts him well clear of his official mark — has run over today's trip and going, and 22 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh; the lack of recent form figures is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: El Regalo
runners_data.note: Ciaran Murphy's five-year-old has a headgear note (blinkers) and ran 24 days ago; a natural hold-up horse with a fades-in-finish flag placed out into midfield by the field composition — his Good-ground record of 0W0P from 15 runs is among the weakest in the field and he is difficult to back on form.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, including a pull-up, El Regalo arrives 24 days fresh and has run over today's trip and going before, but a fourth last time out and 150 lb on his back make improvement hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Uptaurintop
runners_data.note: Alan O'Sullivan (5lb) rides for Eugene O'Sullivan; a genuine hold-up horse by style but realistically racing in midfield given the field size, and his OR of 81 with a placed record of 0W1P from 12 Good-ground runs suggests he runs his race without threatening the frame at this level.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Uptaurintop does show some ability — third last time out and a placed effort four starts back — but an unplaced run among those efforts and a hefty 150 lb to carry will test him, even with distance and going experience in his favour.

runners_data.name: Tasmanian Girl
runners_data.note: Kevin Healy (7lb) is on for Declan Queally whose yard has 2 wins from 7 in the last fortnight; the mare ran 11 days ago and has a headgear note, and despite one win at 2m on Good this record of 1W2P from 15 Good-ground attempts suggests she holds her chance better than her OR of 79 implies, though her natural position at the rear is compromised by the field size.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, including a pull-up, Tasmanian Girl arrives on an 11-day turnaround carrying 148 lb, though she has run over today's distance and going before; our rating of 84 suggests she holds more ability than recent efforts imply, yet the pattern is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Crypto Crash
runners_data.note: Patrick O'Brien (5lb) rides a five-year-old whose form of 00P-69 includes a pull-up; a natural hold-up horse carrying a fades-in-finish flag who is also running at a longer trip than his most recent Good-ground form suggests is ideal, and the redistribution away from the true rear further reduces his chance.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled-up among his recent efforts and a ranking of 13 of 18 on our figures, Crypto Crash is hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns fit enough on a 19-day break.

runners_data.name: Inches Away
runners_data.note: Michael Kenneally (5lb) rides a seven-year-old who was 64 days off the track and has a form string of 0000/0 — five runs without placing; the hold-up profile and fades-in-finish flag combine badly with a slow-pace scenario, and his Good-ground record of 0W0P from seven confirms he has not troubled the scorecard on this surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Inches Away faces a stiff task here; 64 days off the track adds a fitness query, though she does have experience over today's trip and conditions.

runners_data.name: Chesterbaylad
runners_data.note: Josh Williamson (5lb) rides for Helen Markham who has no runners in the last 14 days; the five-year-old was last seen 24 days ago and despite a recent placed run at 2m2f on Good, the fades-in-finish flag is a concern and he is another natural hold-up type squeezed out of his comfort zone by the large field.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15th of 18 on our figures, Chesterbaylad is hard to fancy, though a second three starts back and experience over today's trip and going offer slim encouragement; a return to form is needed here.

runners_data.name: Surviving Murmansk
runners_data.note: Conor Stone-Walsh takes the ride for James Barcoe who has had five runners in 14 days without a winner; last ran just 10 days ago and the OR of 73 is the lowest in the field, though one win at 2m4f on Good shows he can see the trip out and his 14 Good-ground runs (1W2P) suggest more ability than the handicap mark reflects.
runners_data.comment: Surviving Murmansk has been out of the placings in his last four starts, and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures he faces a stiff task here; the one encouragement is he has run over today's trip and going before, and returns on a sharp ten-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: Eaglewood
runners_data.note: The confirmed lone front-runner for Leonard Flynn's yard who last ran 24 days ago; no jockey is listed which is an important market watch, and his Good-ground record of 1W2P from 10 shows he has previously found winning hard despite controlling races — the STYLE_FIT tag signals that if he cannot dominate unchallenged his chance diminishes markedly.
runners_data.comment: Returned to form with a third two starts back, Eaglewood has run over today's trip and going and comes here fit on 24 days' rest; winless in her last five, she'll need to reproduce that best, but 164 lb is no featherweight.

runners_data.name: Lady Victrix
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's yard is 3/20 in the last fortnight and the mare ran just 11 days ago; a hold-up horse carrying a fades-in-finish flag with no jockey listed alongside Eaglewood — both stable entries need jockeys confirmed — and her Good-ground record of 0W0P from five runs on the surface offers little encouragement at OR 77.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a pulled-up effort among them, Lady Victrix arrives on a short 11-day turnaround carrying 146 lb and ranked 17 of 18 on our figures; experience of today's going is modest consolation.

races.paceDynamic: Eaglewood is the sole confirmed front-runner in an 18-runner field and should face no serious pressure for the lead, giving connections the luxury of controlling tempo from the outset on Good ground at Cork over 2m1f. With one horse dictating and no obvious challenger willing to push forward and contest that position, the pace is likely to be honest but not scorching — a sustainable gallop that keeps the race together without creating a true test of stamina. That configuration hands a significant advantage to prominent racers who can track Eaglewood through the race and pounce turning for home, rather than hold-up horses who need a strong pace to manufacture gaps from behind. The field is saturated with genuine hold-up types — Taketwotoone, Inchiquin Maid, Uptaurintop, Tasmanian Girl, Crypto Crash and others have all been redistributed onto the map because they cannot all settle at the true rear in an 18-runner field, but Saint Peregrine is the only other runner with a prominent profile to give Eaglewood any company up front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Eaglewood Controls, Trackers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Eaglewood leads without pressure and Saint Peregrine tracks closely while the pace remains measured.
scenarios.body: Eaglewood sets a comfortable, uncontested gallop and the race develops into a procession for the first circuit, with prominent runners conserving energy directly behind; approaching the last two hurdles the horses who have tracked the pace have first run on the tiring backmarkers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts, Late Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Eaglewood sets a genuinely slow tempo that compresses the field and creates a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: A crawl up front bunches the entire 18-runner field, removing Eaglewood's stamina-grinding advantage and turning the race into a flat-out dash from two out; in that scenario the horses with the best raw speed and those who have accidentally been held up mid-pack benefit.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Injected, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If a second or third horse forces their way to the front early and creates genuine competition for Eaglewood.
scenarios.body: Should the pace become genuinely contentious and the gallop quickens significantly from flagfall, the race turns into a stamina examination over the 2m1f trip; proven stayers with Good-ground form who have been settled in midfield become the beneficiaries as front-runners come back to them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Large Field
scenarios.trigger: If the large 18-runner field causes interference, bunching at hurdles or a messy pace that fragments the race.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners over hurdles on what is a moderately tight circuit, traffic problems are a genuine risk, particularly for horses forced wide or baulked at obstacles in the mid-division; this scenario produces a chaotic finish where form lines are disrupted and lower-rated horses sneak a result.

watchPoints.text: Eaglewood has no jockey listed — confirm the booking before the race as any late change could significantly alter how the front-running role is fulfilled and the entire pace shape of this contest.

Lady Victrix also has no jockey listed; Paul Flynn's yard is active (3/20 in 14 days) and a shrewd booking could indicate market confidence, making this runner worth monitoring in the betting despite modest Good-ground form.

With 18 runners over hurdles at Cork, watch for overcrowding at the early flights — horses like Crypto Crash, Inches Away and Chesterbaylad who are forced into midfield out of role are particularly vulnerable to losing ground or meeting interference at hurdles in the first mile.

Toon Town's recent win at 2m4f on Good and Saint Peregrine's prominent profile make them the two horses most likely to travel into contention behind Eaglewood; any market move on either in a race where tracking the leader is the key tactical position is significant.

The trainer-14-day strike rate for John Patrick Ryan (1/16) is modest, but the combination of Saint Peregrine's prominent style in a race with only one confirmed front-runner means he may get a dream run in second place throughout — his hurdles jumping record (has a fall on his form card) is worth monitoring in the parade ring.

races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Maiden Hurdle

runners_data.name: Beyond Forgiveness
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with unquantified style and a 456-day absence; David Harry Kelly has gone 0/5 in the last 14 days and this horse's P form figure over an unknown trip gives minimal basis for confidence on return.

runners_data.name: Buachaill Jagoes
runners_data.note: Six-year-old returning after 141 days with only a single form figure of 4 to work from; trainer Terence O'Brien is 0/4 in the T14 window and the unknown style makes tactical assessment speculative.

runners_data.name: Carajillo
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by nature but the density of rear-runners in this field means it is unlikely to find its favoured spot; recent form of 8P on Good ground offers no encouragement, and the 0.90 style-fit score reflects meaningful compromise in how this race will be run for it.

runners_data.name: Eye Contact
runners_data.note: Placed once in ten similar-going starts with a clear tendency to fade in the finish; it is a true hold-up runner squeezed into midfield by field composition, and the tongue-tie plus a 13-day turnaround suggest connections are experimenting rather than peaking the horse.

runners_data.name: Lastofthenatives
runners_data.note: Two runs on similar going, both unplaced, with a pulled-up effort and a finishing fade flagged; the 24-day return and unknown upper trip ceiling make this one of the harder horses to anchor to a specific scenario.

runners_data.name: Livio
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner in the race, giving Sean Cleary-Farrell a completely uncontested lead on Good ground at Cork; form includes a win and a third from two similar-going starts, and the Mullins yard's T14 strike-rate of 11/54 is the strongest in the field by a considerable margin.

runners_data.name: Sankofa
runners_data.note: Third on debut over an unknown trip and now 120 days off the track; David Harry Kelly's yard is cold in the T14 window and the lightly-raced unknown style gives little to work with tactically.

runners_data.name: The Monkey Pole
runners_data.note: Has placed twice from six Good-ground starts and stays well over 2m2f based on its best effort, but it is a genuine hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map by field saturation; the 0.90 style-fit score means it needs everything to go its way late, which is unlikely with a slow pace set by Livio.

runners_data.name: Vargas
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's lightly-raced five-year-old returns after 239 days with a P/P- form string; Elliott is 2/41 in the T14 window and the unknown style means any assessment of this runner is largely guesswork on debut-like terms.

runners_data.name: Woodie Wiley
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a form string of P/PS7 and two runs on similar going both unplaced; the 30-day return is reasonable but the fade flag and rear-field tendencies make this an unlikely beneficiary of the race shape Livio is set to create.

runners_data.name: Adifferentballowax
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old has gone 0/3 on similar going with three consecutive finishes of 9-9-15 and a fade flag attached; prominent style means it will be close enough to matter positionally, but the form trend is decidedly discouraging.

runners_data.name: Bury Your Past
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with a lightly-raced profile returning 71 days after a P-5 sequence; unknown style and a cold T14 for trainer Gearoid O'Loughlin mean this is a horse to monitor rather than anchor any scenario around.

runners_data.name: Devine Genius
runners_data.note: A flat-track bumper-type with all flat-course form entries and distances as short as 11f; it is a natural hold-up runner that simply cannot get to the rear in this field, and the step up in both code and trip make this a very difficult ask for a horse that has never placed in nine attempts.

runners_data.name: Johnny Rambo
runners_data.note: Won last time out and was second the time before, both over 2m on Good ground; Alan O'Sullivan's mount is a genuine prominent racer who has proven it can travel close to the pace and quicken, making it the most naturally-suited rival to Livio's expected gallop.

runners_data.name: Pinkarizon
runners_data.note: Nine-place finisher on most recent Good-ground start, with a tongue-tie and hood flag; the 11-day turnaround is short and prior form over shorter trips on varying ground shows no clear step forward, making this a difficult proposition at 2m2f.

runners_data.name: Saporetti
runners_data.note: Brian McMahon's four-year-old has placed twice from three starts on similar going, always racing prominently; the 24-day return is fine and a consistent 3-3-5 form sequence makes this one of the more dependable prominent-style profiles in the field.

runners_data.name: Voice Of Northeast
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a tendency to fade, wearing a tongue-piece; all flat-track entries in its history suggest a fundamental profile mismatch with hurdles at this trip, and the 19-day return adds no particular freshness edge.

runners_data.name: Master Sydney
runners_data.note: Placed four times in twelve similar-going starts and recorded his sole win on Good ground; a genuine hold-up horse who has the most proven record of the rear-runners in the field, though the pace shape set by Livio gives him the smallest possible margin for error late.

runners_data.name: Le Vent d'Ex
runners_data.note: Absent 382 days with only one soft-ground start in its history and no similar-going experience to speak of; M Winters has gone 0/0 in the T14 window and the lengthy layoff makes this a near-impossible runner to price into any shape with confidence.

runners_data.name: Champagne Diamond
runners_data.note: Six-year-old resuming after 364 days with a form string of 555/0-; the one similar-going run produced a tenth and there is a fade flag attached, making this a horse whose return from such a long absence is the central question mark.

runners_data.name: Majestic Horizon
runners_data.note: Placed twice from two similar-going starts over comparable trips and is lightly raced with unknown upside; P J Rothwell is 2/23 in the T14 window, which is modest, but the consistent placing profile and unknown ceiling make this one of the more intriguing unexposed runners.

races.paceDynamic: Livio is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 21-runner maiden hurdle over 2m2f on Good ground at Cork, and with no identified challenger for the lead, Sean Cleary-Farrell's mount should dictate a measured, controlled gallop from the front without any early pressure forcing a tempo that exceeds its natural cruising speed. The prominent types Johnny Rambo and Adifferentballowax will look to track close to the pace, while Saporetti is also a genuine front-of-race runner who can position within striking range. The field carries a heavy concentration of hold-up horses — Devine Genius, Carajillo, The Monkey Pole and Eye Contact are all true rear-of-field types who have been mapped to midfield purely because there is no room for them all to operate from their natural position, meaning their redistribution further compresses the mid-to-rear section of the field and dilutes the effectiveness of any late-run scenario. With a lone, unhurried front-runner setting a sustainable Good-ground gallop and a clutch of prominently-placed types tracking in behind, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race handy and produce a clean jump at the last — a front-to-prominent profile has the clearest tactical edge here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Livio Controls, Handy Types Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Livio leads at a measured clip and the race is won from the first two or three positions off the pace.
scenarios.body: Livio sets a fair but unexaggerated pace on Good ground and the race quickens from two out, rewarding those travelling comfortably just off the leader; Johnny Rambo, fresh from consecutive wins over this course and distance profile, is ideally placed to strike, with Saporetti and Adifferentballowax also threatening from close range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Livio Leads All The Way
scenarios.trigger: If the steady gallop is never truly lifted and Livio's rivals leave their run too late on the Good ground.
scenarios.body: With no horse applying pressure, Livio finds the race run entirely to its own tempo and is never asked a question until deep in the straight, leaving those further back with insufficient time to close; the Mullins yard's T14 figure of 11/54 confirms the stable is in very solid form and Livio's prior front-running win supports this being a genuine match-winner scenario.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the steady fractions nonetheless prove unsustainable and Livio weakens late, gifting ground to mid-division types.
scenarios.body: A flat late-race pace meltdown would theoretically open the door for The Monkey Pole or Master Sydney sweeping from the rear, though both are racing away from their natural position and their redistributed map placement means this outcome relies on horses failing to operate in role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Field Bunches, Chaos Scenario
scenarios.trigger: If the large 21-runner field produces traffic interference, fallers or significant jumping errors that scramble the shape entirely.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners over hurdles on a potentially tight early pace, carnage in midfield is a genuine if unlikely possibility that hands an advantage to the prominently-placed horses who clear trouble early; Majestic Horizon and Bury Your Past, both lightly raced with unknown upside, could emerge if the race falls apart around them.

watchPoints.text: Livio's lead is completely uncontested — watch whether Sean Cleary-Farrell elects to establish a true gallop or dawdles, because a falsely slow pace over 2m2f on Good ground will compress the field and dramatically increase the chance of prominent types like Johnny Rambo and Saporetti overwhelming the leader on the run-in.

With 21 runners negotiating hurdles from the off, monitor the first two flights for jumping errors or crowding in the large field — any incident in the early-mid pack will benefit horses positioned closest to Livio and penalise the hold-up runners already compromised by their redistributed positions.

Johnny Rambo's last two wins were both over 2m on Good ground at a similar level — watch how Alan O'Sullivan positions him relative to Livio from the outset, as getting too far back in a 21-runner field could negate the horse's biggest tactical advantage.

Multiple horses — Devine Genius, Carajillo, Eye Contact and The Monkey Pole — are genuine hold-up types mapped into midfield by necessity; if Livio sets a genuinely slow pace, watch whether any of these attempt to push forward and disrupt their own running style, which could scramble the field order mid-race.

Le Vent d'Ex and Champagne Diamond are both returning from absences exceeding 360 days with minimal known form on this going — watch market moves close to post time, as significant support for either would suggest strong home market intelligence that the form book cannot reflect.

races.name: Jim Ryan Racecourse Services Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Palace Boy

runners_data.comment: Palace Boy has run over today's going before and our rating of 119 puts him right in the mix as a leading danger, but he arrives winless in his last four starts and that 123-day absence is the key question mark against him.

runners_data.name: Miners Bridge
runners_data.note: Missed 398 days between runs but his Good-ground record is genuinely strong at 8/10 with 1W4P, and his best form over 2m-2m4f at this level suggests fitness is the only real question; Phillip Enright can be trusted to give him a sensible ride first time back.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts but has placed twice in that spell — second last time out and a second four starts back — Miners Bridge has going experience in his favour, though a 398-day absence and a hefty 163 lb burden are clear questions to answer.

runners_data.name: Earl Neigh
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer fitted with a tongue-strap, whose recent form shows a P and 0 in the last two starts; Josh Younge claims 7lb which helps the burden, but Andrew Slattery's in-form yard (3/34 T14) provides some encouragement despite the uninspiring recent string.

runners_data.name: Inthenickoftime
runners_data.note: Prominent type with excellent form on Good ground (13/15 runs, 2W7P), though the 59-day absence and an 'O' last time out need contextualising; Simon Torrens partners him over a trip he handles well, and he is one of the most versatile tactical options in the field.
runners_data.comment: Showed plenty when winning and second twice in recent starts, but a pulled up and unplaced effort since cloud his current form; he has run over today's trip and going, though 59 days off and a hefty 160 lb test his readiness.

runners_data.name: Certamen
runners_data.note: Five-year-old prominent racer who has placed 0 wins from 7 runs on Good ground — a consistent under-performer at this level despite regular runs; the tongue-tie has been in use but the form string of 0/56-0 gives little reason for confidence in a 21-runner handicap.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 11th of 20, Certamen faces a stiff task off 159 lb, though he has run over today's going before and a 20-day turnaround suggests he arrives fresh enough to outrun recent unplaced efforts.

runners_data.name: Crowsatedappletart
runners_data.note: Recent winner (1 on last run, Good, 16f) and strong form in similar conditions (3W8P from 15 runs), tongue-tied and in good shape; one of the most likely horses to get into the front rank alongside Jupiter Du Gite and a genuine contender if the race is run at an honest pace.
runners_data.comment: Crowsatedappletart arrives on the back of a win last time out and has run over today's trip and going, making him an obvious threat; the main concern is whether 88 days off has left him short of peak fitness.

runners_data.name: L'As de Watt
runners_data.note: Five-year-old hold-up horse from Philip Fenton's yard with a 64-day break; placed once in four Good-ground runs (0W1P) and the form string of 72-50 is modest, but Brian Hayes is an experienced handler of hold-up types who can deliver a clean late run.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning after 64 days off, L'As de Watt does at least boast a second three starts back to suggest he can mix it at this level, though an unplaced effort last time and 159 lb to carry are real hurdles.

runners_data.name: Calzaghi
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old whose recent form of 980 tells a bleak story; the claiming jockey Calum Hogan claims 5lb and he has placed on Hurdle form previously (2nd twice), but Good-ground returns of 8/14 (1W4P) suggest the trip and conditions are workable if the form is there.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts and ranked 13 of 20 on our ratings, Calzaghi faces a stiff ask under 158 lb, though he has run over today's going before and 32 days off could mean he returns fresher.

runners_data.name: Diamond Tipp
runners_data.note: Prominent type that has pulled up twice in recent starts (P-8P); Jack Kennedy is a positive booking and the tongue-tie is in use, but two recent non-completions and a modest sim-going record (1W6P) make him difficult to trust in a race this competitive.

runners_data.name: Folly Beach
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer who ran just 11 days ago; best form has come at shorter trips (4th over 15f on Good) and he has not won on Good ground (0W1P), so moving up in distance with quick turnaround looks like a tough ask for the Molloy yard.
runners_data.comment: Folly Beach arrives on the back of a third three starts back, and her experience over today's trip and going keeps her firmly in contention — though winless in her last four starts, and 158 lb is the main barrier to reversing recent form.

runners_data.name: Champagne Dawn
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type absent for 280 days — the longest layoff in the field; form before the break includes a win on Good ground but the current string of 8900P shows deterioration, and Danny Mullins' presence is about the most positive element here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulled up most recently, Champagne Dawn returns after a lengthy 280-day absence carrying a hefty 157 lb — significant concerns. He has run over today's trip and going, and a rating of 106 offers a sliver of encouragement for a revival.

runners_data.name: O'Grady Cracker
runners_data.note: Won last time (1, Good, 19f) wearing a visor, though he is flagged as a finisher who fades and his history shows an uneven profile; the 10-day turnaround is quick, J J Slevin is the key booking, and Andrew Slattery's trainer yard is firing (3/34 T14) — one of the more intriguing watch horses despite the fade warning.
runners_data.comment: Beaten in all four starts before that recent win, O'Grady Cracker has experience of today's trip and going, but carrying 157 lb and ranked 16th of 20 on our figures makes him very hard to fancy here.

runners_data.name: Katherine
runners_data.note: Consistent in Good-ground finishes (6th, 9th, 4th, 7th, 7th recent) without threatening to win; a natural hold-up performer in a blinker who has been redistributed to midfield given the field's depth of hold-up types — her actual role will be further back than the map suggests, which tempers her scope to pick up late.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a sixth last time out and a ninth before that, Katherine faces a stiff task ranked 15th of 20 on our figures; experience over today's trip and going offers slim consolation.

runners_data.name: Alentejo
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and fades in finishes; form of 890 in recent starts and has never won on Good ground (0W0P from 6) — a genuine hold-up type placed at the rear in practice, but the redistribution note reflects a crowded backfield, and the fade flag compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with unplaced efforts his most recent form, Alentejo faces a stiff ask under 152 lb; he has run over today's trip and going before, though our rating of 100 suggests he holds some claims despite ranking 14th of 20.

runners_data.name: Imperial Miss
runners_data.note: Five-year-old filly who ran just yesterday (1 day ago) — the freshest turnaround in the race; her best form showed a second over 2m2f Good ground which is a positive trip angle, but racing again so quickly and operating as a genuine hold-up type in a deep rearfield are significant hurdles.

runners_data.name: Boola Times
runners_data.note: Has faded in finishes and wears a tongue-strap and pads; the redistribution to midfield places him ahead of his natural station — he is a true hold-up type in a field that has too many of them, and his sim-going record (0W2P) with recent P in the form is not compelling.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pull-up among those efforts, Boola Times is hard to fancy ranked 17 of 20 on our figures; he does return on a quick 11-day turnaround with going experience in his favour, but the handicapper's 149 lb burden makes life difficult.

runners_data.name: King Ferdinand
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old prominent racer who has a solid Good-ground record (3W4P from 12 runs) but the form string of U66/P0 and a recent non-completion are worrying signs for a horse at this age; Alan O'Sullivan's 5lb claim helps, but the profile looks to be on the slide.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — including a pull-up and an unseating — King Ferdinand arrives here with plenty of questions to answer; he has run over today's trip and going before, and the 18-day turnaround keeps him fresh, but 148 lb is a stiff ask given that patchy recent profile.

runners_data.name: Dictionary Corner
runners_data.note: Five-year-old whose sim-going returns (0W0P, 5/6 runs) show zero wins on Good ground; recent form of P8-66P is deeply uninspiring, and though a natural hold-up type redistributed from the rear, the underlying form offers little optimism regardless of where he settles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and ranked last on our figures, Dictionary Corner faces a stiff task here; two pulled-up efforts among those runs are concerning, though she has run over today's going before and returns after a reasonable 24-day break.

runners_data.name: Scathach
runners_data.note: Hold-up six-year-old with a usable record on Good ground (5/6, 0W1P) including a recent 3rd over 2m2f which matches today's trip exactly; his natural rearward position is crowded in this field, but Scathach has placed at the trip/going combination and deserves respect if finding room.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, ranked 19 of 20 on our figures, and her trainer has yet to land a winner in 22 attempts over the past fortnight — Scathach faces a stiff ask here, though she has run over today's trip and going and returns after a 24-day break.

runners_data.name: Ballyminnion Boy
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with only three recorded runs in the sim-going dataset (3/3, 0W0P) and a fade-in-finishes flag; form of FP-008 is uniformly poor and his redistribution from the rear reflects the overcrowded hold-up section — difficult to find a case for him in a 21-runner heat.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 18 of 20 on our figures, Ballyminnion Boy's recent form — including a fall and a pull-up — makes him hard to fancy, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns on a reasonable 24-day break.

runners_data.name: Jupiter Du Gite
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner (OR 113) and the confirmed front-runner, though the STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) reflects he is racing slightly out of role; history on Soft/Heavy predominantly (best form at Headford/Naas) makes Good ground a minor query, and a Reserve jockey booking is a concern in such a competitive race — he sets the shape but may not finish it.
runners_data.comment: Jupiter Du Gite shaped with real promise when second last time out, and his rating of 119 heads the field here; winless in his last five starts but that runner-up effort 18 days ago reads like a horse coming to the boil, and 169 lb is the one query.

races.paceDynamic: Jupiter Du Gite (OR 113, highest-rated runner) is the confirmed front-runner and, with no dedicated rival to challenge him for the lead in a 21-runner field, he is likely to bowl along at a sustainable, controlled gallop on Good ground at Cork. Behind him, a cluster of prominent types — Crowsatedappletart, Inthenickoftime, Miners Bridge, Palace Boy, Certamen, Diamond Tipp, and King Ferdinand — will press forward and jostle for position through the early stages, creating a genuinely competitive pace picture rather than a dawdle. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all find their natural position; Jupiter Du Gite and Crowsatedappletart are most likely to actually secure the front rank, with Inthenickoftime and Miners Bridge the next most likely to push into the first four, while others must settle slightly further back than ideal. With a sustainable but honest gallop set by a top-rated front-runner and prominent horses working hard to hold position in a big field over 2m2f on Good turf, this race shape strongly favours closers and hold-up horses who can travel smoothly through the field and produce a run in the straight — genuine hold-up performers with good form in similar conditions are best placed to exploit the contested early stages.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite controls a steady-to-fair pace and the prominent pack track him close enough to outstay the hold-up horses in the straight.
scenarios.body: Jupiter Du Gite sets the fractions, Crowsatedappletart and Inthenickoftime sit within two lengths of him throughout, and when the sprint starts at the second-last, the horses with racing room and tactical position overpower those coming from deeper; the Good ground suits a prominent, forward style that does not require maximum gallop to succeed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent group over-races in the big-field scramble for position and ties up in the final half-mile, leaving true hold-up performers to sweep past.
scenarios.body: With Crowsatedappletart, Palace Boy, Certamen, Diamond Tipp, and King Ferdinand all needing prominent ground and 21 runners to navigate, the early pace becomes genuinely contested and those who settle behind it arrive fresher at the last; horses like O'Grady Cracker, L'As de Watt, and Scathach, who can be ridden with restraint, arrive with a late kick that the front-rank horses have burned off.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horses Tire Late
scenarios.trigger: If Jupiter Du Gite sets a stronger pace than expected in the first mile and draws the prominent pack into a battle they cannot sustain over 2m2f.
scenarios.body: The massed prominent group expends energy holding position in the early stages, leaving Crowsatedappletart and Miners Bridge — both of whom have strong Good-ground form — able to sustain their effort longer than rivals who chased harder; Miners Bridge in particular, whose record of 1W4P in Good conditions over this sort of trip is excellent, makes the most of a faltering field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos In Big Field
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding, fallers, or interference disrupts the race shape and scrambles the anticipated running order entirely.
scenarios.body: With 21 runners on a Good surface over 2m2f, interference at hurdles or a loose horse can reshuffle positions beyond any planned strategy; in such chaos the horse with the most versatile style and clearest passage wins, and Inthenickoftime — who has placed across multiple trip and pace scenarios — and Palace Boy, with race-fitness and good visibility for Donoghue, navigate the disruption best.

watchPoints.text: Jupiter Du Gite heads to post with a Reserve jockey and a predominantly Soft/Heavy form profile — if he is headed or pressured before the turn in by the prominent pack, his ability to see out 2m2f on Good ground is genuinely uncertain.

Crowsatedappletart and Inthenickoftime are the two most likely front-rank horses to capitalise if Jupiter Du Gite weakens; watch whether they can secure their natural positions in a 21-runner field at the start, as being shuffled

races.name: Curragh To Curragh Charity Cycle On Saturday August 29th Flat Race

runners_data.name: Awaywego
runners_data.comment: Awaywego makes his debut carrying 168 lb, completely unexposed and with everything still to prove — an open book who could be anything on first appearance.

runners_data.name: Blackwood Joe
runners_data.comment: Blackwood Joe makes his debut carrying 168 lb, entirely unexposed and an unknown quantity — anything he shows here is fresh evidence, and there is plenty of scope for improvement to come.

runners_data.name: Cloneen To The Max
runners_data.comment: Cloneen To The Max shaped with promise when third three starts back, has run over today's trip, and a rating of 80 ranks him fourth in a 17-runner field — a live danger. The 84-day absence and 168 lb burden are the chief concerns.

runners_data.name: Gagaistheboss
runners_data.comment: Gagaistheboss makes his debut carrying 168 lb — unraced and therefore completely unexposed, with his ceiling unknown and plenty of improvement likely to come as he learns his trade.

runners_data.name: Green Style
runners_data.comment: Green Style landed a winner two starts back and, with a speed rating of 124 and our rating of 93 backing his class, he shapes as a genuine threat — though 461 days off the track is the obvious question mark he must answer on return.

runners_data.name: Hoof And Hustle
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and open to improvement, Hoof And Hustle heads here winless in his last two starts, including an eighth on his most recent outing 81 days ago; he carries 168 lb on his return.

runners_data.name: It's Buster's Way
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, It's Buster's Way is yet to score in his most recent start but returns after 58 days freshened up and carries 168 lb, making him one to watch as he builds on limited experience.

runners_data.name: Merci Vieil Ami
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Merci Vieil Ami has had a troubled recent spell — unseated, pulled up, then eighth — yet to win in his last three starts, though he returns fit on just 13 days' rest carrying 168 lb.

runners_data.name: Poet's Sonnet
runners_data.comment: Unexposed and open to improvement, Poet's Sonnet returns from a 267-day absence yet to win in recent starts; lightly raced, he carries 168 lb and the lengthy break leaves plenty to assess.

runners_data.name: S T Hamo
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, S T Hamo nevertheless heads this 17-runner field as our top-rated runner, and a fourth last time out suggests he's knocking on the door; fit enough at 18 days between runs, he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 168 lb is a stiff burden to carry.

runners_data.name: Tale Of Intrigue
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last four starts, Tale Of Intrigue at least showed he's knocking on the door with a third two starts back, and lightly raced, he remains open to further improvement; the 168 lb burden is the query here.

runners_data.name: Red Shea
runners_data.comment: Red Shea makes his debut carrying 165 lb, wholly unexposed and open to any amount of improvement — an unknown quantity on first ask.

runners_data.name: Rinnaseer Beauty
runners_data.comment: Rinnaseer Beauty makes his racecourse debut carrying 165 lb, unexposed and with everything still to learn — a gelding open to significant improvement as connections get their first read on his ability.

runners_data.name: Bonnie Loch
runners_data.comment: Bonnie Loch makes her debut carrying 161 lb, wholly unexposed and open to improvement — a mare with everything still to prove but, equally, everything still to show.

runners_data.name: Cloudy Rosie
runners_data.comment: Cloudy Rosie is yet to win in her last three starts but has been placed in all of them — second last time out, and third in each of the two prior runs — and this lightly raced mare looks open to improvement after a 148-day break carrying 161 lb.

runners_data.name: Echoes Of Jane
runners_data.comment: Consistently placed in her last three completed starts — second last time out, and third twice before that — Echoes Of Jane brings solid recent form and has run over today's trip and going; the concern is that she remains yet to win in recent starts.

runners_data.name: Free A Minute
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with two pulled-up efforts among them, Free A Minute makes a hard case — though 57 days off could mean a freshened-up run, and she has experience over today's trip to draw on.
